sentences.text:
24/07/2017 :-
 Shri Vinayak Balchandani, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Vikas Jain, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State.
Arguments heard.

Aggrieved by order dated 27/06/2017 passed in criminal revision No.32/2017 by III ASJ, Dhar whereby the learned Revisional Court has confirmed the order of trial Court dated 13/05/2017 passed by JMFC, Dhar in criminal case No.2803/2010 dismissing the application of petitioner for recalling the Public Analyzed and a Panch witness - Shailesh Gupta, the petitioner has preferred the present petition.
2. It is submitted by the petitioner that he is being prosecuted for the charge under Section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

After completion of the prosecution evidence, at the stage of defence, the petitioner has filed an application under Section 243 readwith Section 293 of Cr.P.C. for calling the Public Analyst, State Food Laboratory, Bhopal and one Shailesh Gupta.
The application was dismissed by the learned trial Court and learned Revisional Court has confirmed the order of trial Court.
3. It is submitted that two reports were filed by the prosecution before the trial Court to prove the adulteration but there is difference between both the reports about contemptuous substance.
State Food Laboratory has found the sample according to the standards but the Central Food Laboratory found that the sample was of sub-standard.
It is further submitted that he has challenged the process adopted by the Food Inspector while taking the sample.
For these reason statement of the Public Analyst and the Panch witness - Shailesh Gupta were necessary to prove his defence.
He filed an application for calling both of them as defence witness.

4. The application was dismissed by the trial Court considering the provisions of Section 13 (5) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Section 4 of the Evidence Act which provides that the report of Central Food Laboratory supersedes report of State Food Laboratory, therefore, no useful purpose would be achieved by calling public analyst.
5. Finding of trial Court is according to the law and the Revisional Court has correctly up-held the same.
No ground for interference is made out in this finding.
6. The petitioner has disputed the procedure adopted by the Food Inspector while taking the sample.

To rebut the statement of Food Inspector, he wants to produce or examine the Panch Rajendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through ... on 24 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65418453/
1 witness - Shailesh Gupta in his defence.

sentences.text: The application is filed before the trial Court and learned trial Court did not assign any reason for turning down his request.

The reason assigned by the learned Revisional Court that as the trial Court has decided the case on the basis of evidence and documents available on record, therefore, there is no need to call or examine Shailesh Gupta, does not appear to be correct.
7. The petitioner has challenged the procedure since the charge framed against him.
He wants to fortify his challenge by producing defence evidence.
He filed application for this purpose promptly on time.
The trial Court did not grant any opportunity for defence evidence.
The learned Revisional Court also ignored this fact.

Reasons assigned by the Courts below are not justified to deprive the petitioner from adducing the evidence in his defence and to establish the fact stated or controverted by him during course of the trial.
8. In my considered opinion and in the interest of justice, petitioner is entitled for getting an opportunity for adducing the evidence in his defence for the issue raised earlier in the trial.
In view of this, present petition is allowed in part.

The order of learned Revisional Court so far as it relates to calling the Public Analyst as defence witness is confirmed but it is set-aside to the extent, it relates to calling of Panch witness - Shailesh Gupta.
9.

Learned trial Court is directed to grant the petitioner opportunity of adducing evidence in his defence and if necessary to extend assistance of the Court for calling of the witness after following the due process of law.
10.
With the aforesaid, the present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
C.C. as per rules.

(Virender Singh) Judge Aiyer*
